result.question: Why can't David go into battle?

readings.answer: To prevent the lamp of Israel from being extinguished.
readings.support: so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished

readings.answer: Because his men forbade him from going out to battle.
readings.support: Then David’s men swore to him | You must never again go out with us to battle

readings.answer: Because he had needed help in battle (was in danger).
readings.support: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid

assessments.reason: “so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished” conveys the risk to David’s life, matching the key’s “Risk of being killed.”

“Then David’s men swore to him, ‘You must never again go out with us to battle’” explains his incapacity as their prohibition, which is accurate though it gives the immediate cause rather than the underlying risk stated in the key.
“Abishai … came to his aid” implies David was in danger in battle, aligning with the key’s reason that he faced the risk of being killed.
